Aura.description: A cleric who serves a chaotic, evil, good, or lawful deity radiates an especially strong aura that matches the deity's alignment. Clerics without a specific patron deity who select the Chaotic, Evil, Good, or Lawful domain likewise emanate a potent aura aligned with that domain.

Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells.description: A cleric is unable to cast spells whose alignment directly opposes either his own alignment or that of his deity (if applicable). For instance, a good cleric (or a neutral cleric devoted to a good deity) is barred from casting evil spells. A spell's alignment association is identified by the chaos, evil, good, and law descriptors listed in the spell's details.
Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells.seedName: Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells (Cleric)

Deity, Domains, and Domain Spells.description: Select a deity for your cleric. The chosen deity shapes the cleric's alignment, available magic, personal values, and public perception. Alternatively, a cleric may serve no specific deity at all. When a deity's typical followers belong to a particular race, the cleric must share that race to worship that deity. (Other races may revere the deity casually, but cannot serve as its clerics.) After settling on an alignment and deity, pick two domains from those associated with that deity. Though all clerics of a given faith share devotion to their god, individual clerics focus on different facets of the deity's portfolio. An alignment domain (Chaos, Evil, Good, or Law) may only be chosen if the cleric's alignment corresponds to it. Clerics without a patron deity still choose two domains reflecting their spiritual focus and aptitudes, and the alignment domain restriction still applies. Each domain provides access to one domain spell per spell level the cleric can cast (beginning at 1st level) along with a granted power. The cleric receives the granted powers of both chosen domains. Since a cleric has access to two domain spells at each available spell level, he prepares one of the two each day in his domain spell slot. If a domain spell does not appear on the cleric spell list, the cleric can only prepare it in the domain spell slot. Domain spells and granted powers are detailed under Cleric Domains.

Spells.description: A cleric wields divine magic (the same category of spells used by druids, paladins, and rangers), drawing from the cleric spell list. His alignment may, however, prevent him from casting certain spells that conflict with his moral or ethical principles; see Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells. A cleric must select and prepare spells ahead of time. Preparing or casting a spell requires a Wisdom score of at least 10 + the spell's level (Wisdom 10 for 0-level spells, Wisdom 11 for 1st-level spells, and so on). The saving throw DC against a cleric's spell equals 10 + the spell's level + the cleric's Wisdom modifier. As with other spellcasting classes, a cleric can only cast a limited number of spells of each level per day. His base daily allotment is shown in the class table, and a high Wisdom score grants additional bonus spells per day. The cleric also receives one domain spell of each castable spell level, starting at 1st level. When filling a domain spell slot, the prepared spell must belong to one of the cleric's two domains. Clerics do not learn spells from books or scrolls, nor do they study to prepare them. Rather, they pray or meditate to receive their spells, granted through the strength of their faith or direct divine inspiration. Each cleric must designate a specific time of day to spend 1 hour in quiet prayer or contemplation in order to refresh his daily spell allotment. Good clerics typically perform this devotion at dawn or noon, while evil clerics tend to do so at dusk or midnight. Resting has no bearing on a cleric's ability to prepare spells. A cleric may prepare and cast any spell from the cleric spell list as long as he can cast spells of that level, but he must decide which spells to prepare during his daily meditation.

Spontaneous Casting.description: A good cleric (or a neutral cleric who worships a good deity) can convert stored spell energy into healing magic that was not prepared in advance. The cleric may sacrifice any prepared spell that is not a domain spell to cast any cure spell of equal or lower level (a cure spell being any spell with "cure" in its name). For instance, a good cleric with command prepared (a 1st-level spell) could give it up to cast cure light wounds (also 1st level). Clerics of good deities have this ability because of their exceptional facility with positive energy. Conversely, an evil cleric (or a neutral cleric serving an evil deity) cannot convert prepared spells into cure spells, but may instead convert them into inflict spells (any spell with "inflict" in its name). A cleric who is neither good nor evil - and whose deity is likewise neutral - may convert spells into either cure or inflict spells (player's choice), based on whether the cleric has greater aptitude with positive or negative energy. This choice is permanent once made and also governs whether the cleric turns or commands undead.

Turn or Rebuke Undead.description: Every cleric, regardless of alignment, possesses the ability to influence undead creatures (including skeletons, zombies, ghosts, and vampires) by channeling the force of faith through a holy (or unholy) symbol. A good cleric (or a neutral cleric devoted to a good deity) can turn or destroy undead. An evil cleric (or a neutral cleric devoted to an evil deity) instead rebukes or commands such creatures, compelling them to cower before divine authority. A neutral cleric of a neutral deity must decide whether the turning ability operates as a good cleric's or an evil cleric's; this choice is permanent. This decision also determines whether the cleric spontaneously casts cure or inflict spells. A cleric can attempt to turn undead a number of times per day equal to 3 + his Charisma modifier. Having 5 or more ranks in Knowledge (religion) grants a +2 bonus on turning checks against undead.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: Clerics are proficient with all simple weapons, all armor types (light, medium, and heavy), and all shields except tower shields. Each deity has a favored weapon, and clerics take pride in wielding it. A cleric who selects the War domain gains the Weapon Focus feat for that deity's favored weapon as a bonus feat. If the favored weapon is a martial weapon, the cleric also receives the corresponding Martial Weapon Proficiency feat as a bonus feat.

overrides.alignment: A cleric alignment must be within one step of his deity
overrides.description: Evidence of divine power permeates the world - visible in pristine wilderness, righteous campaigns, towering cathedrals, and the devotion of the faithful. Gods, much like mortals, span the full spectrum from kind to cruel, passive to meddlesome, straightforward to enigmatic. Yet the gods typically act through mortal agents - their clerics. Benevolent clerics mend wounds, shield the innocent, and deliver justice. Malevolent clerics plunder, ravage, and undermine. A cleric channels divine authority to enact the will of a deity. And if that divine power also elevates the cleric's own standing, that is simply to be expected. A cleric's quests should ideally serve the interests of the deity, at least broadly. A good cleric, for instance, aids those who suffer. If such righteous deeds also bolster the standing of the cleric's god or temple, all the better. An evil cleric works to expand both personal influence and the reach of the deity, so that others come to respect and dread them both. Clerics may from time to time receive directives - or at least guidance - from religious superiors, tasking them with missions on behalf of the faith. Such missions are fairly compensated, and the church can be particularly generous with spellcasting services or divine magic items as payment. Naturally, clerics are also individuals with their own motivations, and they may pursue adventure for any of the usual personal reasons.

classFeatures.description: Clerics are proficient with all simple weapons, with all types of armor (light, medium, and heavy), and with shields (except tower shields). Every deity has a favored weapon, and his or her clerics consider it a point of pride to wield that weapon. A cleric who chooses the War domain receives the Weapon Focus feat related to that weapon as a bonus feat. He also receives the appropriate Martial Weapon Proficiency feat as a bonus feat, if the weapon falls into that category. See Chapter 5: Feats for details.

classFeatures.description: A cleric casts divine spells (the same type of spells available to the druid, paladin, and ranger), which are drawn from the cleric spell list. However, his alignment may restrict him from casting certain spells opposed to his moral or ethical beliefs; see Chaotic, Evil, Good, and Lawful Spells, below. A cleric must choose and prepare his spells in advance. To prepare or cast a spell, a cleric must have a Wisdom score equal to at least 10 + the spell level (Wis 10 for 0-level spells, Wis 11 for 1st-level spells, and so forth). The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a cleric's spell is 10 + the spell level + the cleric's Wisdom modifier. Like other spellcasters, a cleric can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. His base daily spell allotment is given in the class table. In addition, he receives bonus spells per day if he has a high Wisdom score. A cleric also gets one domain spell of each spell level he can cast, starting at 1st level. When a cleric prepares a spell in a domain spell slot, it must come from one of his two domains Deities, Domains, and Domain Spells, below). Clerics do not acquire their spells from books or scrolls, nor do they prepare them through study. Instead, they meditate or pray for their spells, receiving them through their own strength of faith or as divine inspiration. Each cleric must choose a time at which he must spend 1 hour each day in quiet contemplation or supplication to regain his daily allotment of spells. Typically, this hour is at dawn or noon for good clerics and at dusk or midnight for evil ones. Time spent resting has no effect on whether a cleric can prepare spells. A cleric may prepare and cast any spell on the cleric spell list, provided that he can cast spells of that level, but he must choose which spells to prepare during his daily meditation.
classFeatures.name: Spells

classFeatures.description: A good cleric (or a neutral cleric of a good deity) can channel stored spell energy into healing spells that the cleric did not prepare ahead of time. The cleric can "lose" any prepared spell that is not a domain spell in order to cast any cure spell of the same spell level or lower (a cure spell is any spell with "cure" in its name). For example, a good cleric who has prepared command (a 1st-level spell) may lose command in order to cast cure light wounds (also a 1st-level spell). Clerics of good deities can cast cure spells in this way because they are especially proficient at wielding positive energy. An evil cleric (or a neutral cleric of an evil deity), on the other hand, can't convert prepared spells to cure spells but can convert them to inflict spells (an inflict spell is one with "inflict" in its name). A cleric who is neither good nor evil and whose deity is neither good nor evil can convert spells to either cure spells or inflict spells (player's choice), depending on whether the cleric is more proficient at wielding positive or negative energy. Once the player makes this choice, it cannot be reversed. This choice also determines whether the cleric turns or commands undead. Exceptions: All lawful neutral clerics of Wee Jas (goddess of death and magic) convert prepared spells to inflict spells, not cure spells. All clerics of St. Cuthbert (god of retribution) and all nonevil clerics of Obad-Hai (god of nature) convert prepared spells to cure spells, not inflict spells.

Spells associated with particular alignments are indicated by the chaos, evil, good, and law descriptors in their spell descriptions.

classFeatures.description: Choose a deity for your cleric. Sample deities are listed in the class table. The cleric's deity influences his alignment, what magic he can perform, his values, and how others see him. You may also choose for your cleric to have no deity. If the typical worshipers of a deity include the members of a race, a cleric must be of the indicated race to choose that deity as his own. (The god may have occasional worshipers of other races, but not clerics.) When you have chosen an alignment and a deity for your cleric, choose two domains from among those given in the class table. While the clerics of a particular religion are united in their reverence for their deity, each cleric emphasizes different aspects of the deity's interests. You can select an alignment domain (Chaos, Evil, Good, or Law) for your cleric only if his alignment matches that domain. If your cleric is not devoted to a particular deity, you still select two domains to represent his spiritual inclinations and abilities. The restriction on alignment domains still applies. Each domain gives your cleric access to a domain spell at each spell level he can cast, from 1st on up, as well as a granted power. Your cleric gets the granted powers of both the domains selected. With access to two domain spells at a given spell level, a cleric prepares one or the other each day in his domain spell slot. If a domain spell is not on the cleric spell list, a cleric can prepare it only in his domain spell slot. Domain spells and granted powers are given in Cleric Domains. For example, Jozan is a 1st-level cleric of Pelor. He chooses Good and Healing (from Pelor's domain options) as his two domains. He gets the granted powers of both his selected domains. The Good domain allows him to cast all spells with the good descriptor at +1 caster level (as if he were one level higher as a cleric) as a granted power, and it gives him access to protection from evil as a 1st-level domain spell. The Healing domain allows him to cast all healing subschool spells of the conjuration school at +1 caster level as a granted power, and it gives him access to cure light wounds as a 1st-level domain spell. When Jozan prepares his spells, he gets one 1st-level spell for being a 1st-level cleric, one bonus 1st-level spell for having a high Wisdom score (15), and one domain spell. The domain spell must be one of the two to which he has access, either protection from evil or cure light wounds.
